title: 11 Best Event Management Platforms in 2026
summary: Best event management platforms for 2026, compared by features, pricing, and best use case. See which one fits your team's events and how InEvent stacks up
body_markdown:
[Tech and Trends](https://inevent.com/blog/tech-and-trends)


###### Posted on October 16, 2026


Planning an event often means running it across four or five different tools. Registration sits in one app and badges in another. The livestream needs its own login, and someone on the team spends the week before the event copying attendee lists between them. The best event management platforms solve this by running the whole event from one place.


We compared 11 event management platforms for 2026. For each one, we cover what it’s best for, its key features, pricing, and pros and cons. The list covers all-in-one platforms for conferences and hybrid events, plus lighter event ticketing tools for smaller gatherings. Start with the comparison table, then read the full reviews.


A quick disclosure: InEvent makes one of the platforms on this list. We list cons for every tool, our own included.

##


**What Is an Event Management Platform?**


An event management platform is software that runs an event from the first invite to the final report. It combines the event website, registration and ticketing, check-in, the event app, live or virtual sessions, networking, and analytics. Teams work from one attendee database instead of syncing separate tools, which saves time and keeps data accurate.


Most event management platforms are cloud-based, so your team can manage events online from any office or venue. They are also different from general event planning tools like task boards and chat apps. Those tools help your team organize its own work, but they can’t sell a ticket or print a badge. An all-in-one event platform also handles everything attendees see. If you mainly need checklists and scheduling, see our roundup of **[event planning software](https://inevent.com/blog/events/event-planning-software.html)** .

##


**2. Cvent**


Best for: large enterprises running many events plus venue sourcing.


Cvent is one of the longest-established names in enterprise event management. Its suite covers registration, marketing, an attendee hub for virtual sessions, on-site check-in, and a large venue sourcing network for hotels and meeting spaces.


**Key features:**


- Registration, event websites, and email marketing


- Venue sourcing and hotel room block management


- Attendee hub for virtual and hybrid content


- On-site check-in, badge printing, and lead capture


**Pricing:** custom quote, usually by module.


**Pros:** very broad feature set; a strong meeting planning platform for venue and hotel sourcing.


**Cons:** reviewers often mention a steep learning curve; costs can grow as you add modules.


### **3. Bizzabo**


Best for: marketing-led B2B conferences.


Bizzabo is one of the best-known event marketing platforms. It treats each event as a marketing channel, with branded websites, registration, an event app, and engagement data that feeds marketing systems. Its on-site tools include badge printing and wearable networking devices.


Key features:


- Website builder and registration


- Event app with agenda, networking, and engagement


- On-site check-in and badge printing


- Marketing integrations and engagement analytics


**Pricing** : custom quote.


**Pros:** polished attendee experience; good fit for marketing teams.


**Cons:** quote-based pricing; can be more than small events need.


### **4. Whova**


Best for: conferences that want a strong event app and attendee engagement.


Whova is best known for its event app, which gives attendees an agenda, a networking directory, community boards, and gamification. Organizers also get registration, check-in, and exhibitor tools.


**Key features:**


- Event app with agenda, messaging, and community boards


- Registration, ticketing, and check-in


- Exhibitor and sponsor exposure tools


- Virtual and hybrid session hosting


Pricing: custom quote, usually per event.


Pros: Attendees tend to download the app and keep using it; quick to set up.


Cons: branding and design control are more limited than enterprise platforms.


### **5. Swapcard**


Best for: trade shows and expos where networking and exhibitors drive value.


Swapcard is event networking software built around AI-powered matchmaking, meeting scheduling, and exhibitor lead capture. It suits shows where attendees come mainly to meet buyers, sellers, and partners.


**Key features:**


- AI recommendations for people, exhibitors, and sessions


- Meeting scheduling between attendees and exhibitors


- Exhibitor portals and lead retrieval


- Event app for in-person and virtual attendees


**Pricing:** custom quote.


**Pros:** strong networking and exhibitor value; built for large shows.


**Cons:** Check how registration, badge printing, and on-site operations fit your setup before you buy.


### **6. RingCentral Events**


Best for: virtual and hybrid events at companies already using RingCentral.


RingCentral Events grew out of the Hopin events product, which RingCentral acquired in 2023. It offers a virtual venue with stages, sessions, an expo hall and networking, plus registration and on-site check-in tools.


Key features:


- Virtual venue with stage, sessions, expo, and networking


- Registration and ticketing


- On-site check-in for hybrid events


- Integration with RingCentral’s video and communications tools


**Pricing:** published plans for smaller events and a quote for enterprise.


**Pros:** strong virtual experience; natural fit for RingCentral customers.


**Cons:** in-person tools are less mature than its virtual features.


### **7. Zoom Events**


**Best for:** webinars, online courses, and virtual event series.


Zoom Events builds on the video tool most attendees already know. It adds ticketing, registration, multi-session agendas and an event hub to Zoom’s meeting and webinar features.


**Key features:**


- Ticketing and registration for single or multi-session events


- Webinars, breakout rooms, polls, and Q&A


-


- Recordings and on-demand content


**Pricing:** paid plans, often added to an existing Zoom account.


**Pros:** familiar to almost every attendee; reliable video.


**Cons:** limited on-site tools such as badge printing and lead retrieval for in-person events.


### 8. Sched


**Best for:** agenda-heavy conferences, meetings and festivals on a budget.


Sched is lightweight conference management software built around the schedule. Attendees build personal agendas in a desktop and mobile app, and organizers manage speakers, sessions and room changes in one place.


**Key features:**


- Schedule builder with personal attendee agendas


- Integrated paid registration


- Desktop and mobile event app


- In-person, hybrid and virtual session support


**Pricing:** tiered plans, with special pricing for nonprofit and educational organizations.


**Pros:** affordable; very easy for attendees to use.


**Cons:** lighter on marketing, sponsor tools and on-site badge printing.


### 9. Eventbrite


**Best for:** public, community and entertainment events that need ticket sales and discovery.


Eventbrite is one of the best-known ticketing websites for public events. Many people browse Eventbrite to find local events, so a listing can bring in buyers who have never heard of you.


**Key features:**


- Event pages and online ticket sales


- Event discovery marketplace


- Email and social promotion tools


- Mobile app for check-in and sales tracking


**Pricing:** free for free events; fees apply to paid tickets.


**Pros:** fast setup; built-in audience.


**Cons:** fees add up on paid tickets; not designed for complex B2B conferences with sponsors and hybrid sessions.


### 10. Eventzilla


**Best for:** small and mid-size events that need low-cost registration.


Eventzilla covers the registration side well. Organizers can set up ticket types, discounts and payment options quickly, then check people in from a mobile app.


**Key features:**


- Registration pages with paid, free and donation tickets
- Promo codes and group discounts
- Online and offline payments
- Mobile check-in and sales reports


**Pricing:** per-registration fee.


**Pros:** low cost; simple to run.


**Cons:** limited networking, streaming and enterprise features.


### 11. TicketSource


**Best for:** theaters, venues and performances that sell seated tickets.


TicketSource is an online ticketing and box office system. It lets venues combine website, social media and in-house bookings, and it can even run a telephone box office.


**Key features:**


- Seating plan creator so buyers can choose seats
- Box office for phone and in-person sales
- Print-at-home or posted tickets
- Door entry and attendee lists


**Pricing:** free for organizers, with booking fees mainly paid by ticket buyers.


**Pros:** no cost to organizers; strong for seated venues.


**Cons:** built for ticketing, not for conferences, networking, or hybrid events.


##


How Do You Create Tickets for an Event?


To create tickets for an event, choose a ticketing or event management platform, then set up your event page with the date, venue, and description. Add ticket types with prices, quantities, and sale dates. Connect a payment method, publish the page, and share the link. Attendees receive a QR ticket for check-in.


Here’s the process step by step:


1. **Pick your tool.** Event registration software is enough for simple ticket sales. Choose a full platform if you also need badges, an app, or hybrid sessions.


2. **Build the event page.** Add the name, date, time zone, venue or streaming link, agenda, and your branding.


3. **Create ticket types.** Common types are early bird, general admission, VIP, group, speaker, and exhibitor. Set a price, a quantity cap, and a sales window for each one.


4. **Add registration questions.** Ask only what you’ll use, such as job title, dietary needs, or session choices.


5. **Connect payments and taxes.** Link your payment processor, set the currency, and add promo codes if needed.


6. **Publish, share, and test.** Buy a test ticket yourself to check the confirmation email and the QR code before you promote the event.


Want to compare tools built just for selling tickets? See our **[comparison of ticketing platforms](https://inevent.com/blog/events/ticketing-platforms.html)** .


##


Other Event Planner Tools to Use Alongside a Platform


Monday.com, Slack, ProjectManager and Everwall don’t run registration or check-in. Many teams still use these event planner tools for internal work around the event:


- **Monday.com:** project boards, timelines, and automations to track task ownership.


- **Slack:** fast team chat during planning and live coordination on event day.


- **ProjectManager:** Gantt charts and resource planning for large, multi-team events.
- **Everwall:** a live social media wall that shows attendee posts on venue screens.


Before adding one, check whether your event platform already covers the job. Every extra tool is one more login and one more attendee list to keep up to date.


##


How Do You Choose the Best Event Management Platform?


To choose the best event management platform, list every event format and task you need to cover. Then shortlist platforms that handle everything in one system. Compare ease of use, integrations, on-site tools, support, and total cost. Finally, run a demo using your own event and read verified reviews.


Check these eight factors on every shortlisted platform:


- **Event formats:** can one hybrid event platform serve in-person, virtual, and hybrid audiences without rebuilding the event? Our **[Virtual & Hybrid Events](https://inevent.com/en/go-beyond-virtual-hybrid-vh-events.php)** solution shows what that looks like in practice.


- **Ease of use:** your team should be able to build a registration page without vendor help.


- **Brand control:** an event website builder that matches your brand matters, because the event page is the first thing attendees see.


- **On-site operations:** look for badge printing and check-in, kiosks, session scanning, and event lead retrieval for exhibitors.


- **Attendee engagement:** test the app’s polls, Q&A, gamification and AI matchmaking, plus how well the virtual event platform keeps remote guests involved.


- **Data and reporting:** event analytics should show registrations, attendance, and engagement in one view, so you can prove event ROI.


- **Integrations and security:** confirm the CRM, marketing automation, and single sign-on connections you need. Enterprise event management also requires security and compliance documentation.


- **Support and total cost:** check support hours across time zones, and compare the platform’s price against all the tools it replaces.


Our event strategists recommend mapping your full event lifecycle before you book demos, from first invite to post-event survey. Then score each platform against that map rather than against its own feature list.


**Team Tip:** *In every demo, ask the vendor to import your last event’s real attendee CSV and print three test badges: VIP, speaker, and exhibitor. Messy real data, such as long job titles, accented names, and missing company fields, shows within minutes whether the import and badge templates will hold up on event day.*


##


Is One Platform Better Than Separate Event Tools?


Yes, one event platform is better for most teams that run more than a few events a year or any hybrid event. One system removes duplicate data entry, keeps attendee records in sync, and gives you one report. Separate tools only make sense for a single small, simple event.


Separate tools look cheaper at first, but each one comes with its own subscription, login, training and support contact. Each also exports its own version of the attendee list, and someone has to reconcile them. That work grows with every sponsor, paid ticket type, remote audience, and extra event you add.


##


Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best event management platform?


The best event management platform is the one that runs your whole event from one system: registration, ticketing, check-in, badge printing, streaming, networking, and analytics. For conferences and hybrid events, look for an all-in-one platform like InEvent. Simple ticketed events may only need a basic ticketing tool. Compare by event format, attendee count and total cost.


### Which event management platform is the most popular?


The most popular event management platforms fall into two groups: ticketing marketplaces for public events, and all-in-one platforms for corporate conferences and hybrid events. InEvent, for example, has powered more than 1.2 million events in 182+ countries. Popularity matters less than fit, so choose the platform that covers every part of your event.


### What is event management software?


Event management software is a tool that helps teams plan, promote, and run events. It handles tasks like registration, ticketing, attendee communication, check-in, and reporting. Some products cover one task, such as ticket sales. An event management platform covers the whole event, including the event app, streaming, and networking.


### How do you choose event management software?


To choose event management software, start with your event types, attendee numbers, and must-have features. Shortlist two or three tools that cover all of them, then compare ease of use, integrations, support, and total cost. Test each one in a demo with your own event data before you sign.


### What are the best event management apps?


The best event management apps give attendees an agenda, networking, live polls, and a mobile ticket in one place. Organizers should also get real-time check-in data and engagement reports. Choose an app built into your event platform, like the InEvent mobile app, so attendee data never has to sync between tools.


##
